rows: A CO-OP observer reported 62 mph wind gusts which knocked large limbs off some trees and blew a shed on a pier into the harbor.

A resident first noticed a tornado over an open field approximately 1-2 miles east of U.S. Highway 77 just south of FM 491. The tornado moved westward toward U.S. Highway 77 and lifted as it approached the Highway, then dissipated. The tornado was on the ground approximately 3 to…

The husband of a CO-OP observer reported hail fell at their residence near the center of town on Copano Road in Port Mansfield. The hail occurred when an isolated thunderstorm moved through the area. The thunderstorm was triggered by a cold front moving through Deep South Texas.

Emergency management officials reported a brief touchdown of a small tornado in western Willacy County, likely between Sebastian and Lyford. The tornado produced some damage, but details were not known.

A Raymondville Volunteer Fire Department employee reported penny size hail fell in the city of Raymondville during a thunderstorm that moved through Willacy County. The Willacy County Emergency Manager also reported penny size hail had fallen in the city of Raymondville during th…

A microburst from a cluster of thunderstorms moving through Raymondville toward Lyford rolled a new but unsecured mobile home just west of Raymondville. Nearby, several fences were blown down, and the door to an industrial building was blown in. Farther south, at about the same t…
A trained spotter reported hail up to golf ball size in diameter during a thunderstorm which moved north between Raymondville and Perlita during the afternoon of June first.
KRGV Television station reported that the public had reported a brief touchdown of a tornado near the town of Willamar. No damage was reported and there werenï¿½ï¿½ï¿½t any homes in the area.

The Port Mansfield Harbor Master reported wind gusts up to 60 miles per hour were measured during a strong thunderstorm which moved through Port Mansfield in the early afternoon. Duration of gusts estimated by proxy with similar conditions as the line passed Laguna Madre-side loc…

Trees and large limbs were blown down on various streets in Raymondville. Time and duration are estimated by radar, based on core of estimated winds between 50 and 52 knots a few thousand feet above the surface.
Texas Military Forces reported a small, brief touch down near Highway 77 north of Raymondville. No damage was reported as of this writing.

A friend of an NWS employee reported Golfball size hail in Raymondville, some which caused dents and dings to several vehicles parked outside, as the first of two hailstorms scooted through Willacy County during the mid afternoon of May 15th, 2011.
A spotter reported penny size hail fell for approximately 3 or 4 minutes east of San Perlita near the intersection of FM 3142 and Highway 186.

Willacy County emergency manager relayed a report of a tornado on the Yturria Ranch, just east of Highway 77 in the northern portion of the county. There was a brief touch down and debris seen, but no damage reported.
Willacy County emergency manager reported penny to golf ball size hail across Raymondville.
Public reported golf ball size hail on Highway 77 near Lyford.
Tornado reported near Wal-Mart in Raymondville. Tornado touched down briefly. No damage reported.
Emergency manager reported winds from 50 to 60 mph in Raymondville.

After an initial report of baseball to softball sized hail in Sebastian, visual evidence from an NWS storm survey indicated no discernible hail impact in Sebastian. Estimated size was penny sized based on conversations with affected residents. the hail lasted up to 10 minutes.
Willacy County emergency manager reported golfball size hail 2 miles south of Raymondville.
Public reported nickel size hail near Raymondville, about 2 miles east of Highway 77.

The Willacy County Emergency Manager reported quarter size hail near Yturria. The public reported quarter size hail on the north side of Raymondville. Each report was from the same hail core, which moved quickly northeast of town and may have dropped larger hail over rural locati…

Nickel sized hail was reported at the intersection of 1st St. and Tampico Ave., also on the north side of town, at 434 PM CDT, by the public. Report was relayed to the NWS by a local weather broadcaster.

A meteorologist from the U.S. National Weather Service in Brownsville surveyed the damage, which occurred in and around the San Perlita area. The damage was found to be the result of damaging straight line winds, with wind speeds estimated between 70 and 80 mph.||Damage appeared …
Willacy County Sheriff's Department reported golf ball size hail fell on FM 490, 6 miles west of Willamar at 6 pm.
Nickel to quarter sized hail fell in San Perlita. Event time based on radar.
Raymondville Police Department reported estimated 60 mph winds when the storm came through.
The public reported that a barn was destroyed 5 miles west of Raymondville. The barn also crushed a car. Winds were estimated at 70 to 80 mph.

Raymondville Police Department reported that the Precinct 1 garage west of Raymondville on Highway 186 sustained heavy damage from straight line thunderstorm winds. The garage doors were blown down and a section of hurricane fencing near the garage was also blown down.
Local law enforcement reported a semi truck blown over at FM 1015 and Highway 186.
Local law enforcement reported trees down in the city of Lyford.

Willacy County EM reported a telephone pole blown down at 100 East Sunset Avenue in Raymondville and at the intersection of FM 1762 and Business 77 in Raymondville. Peak winds were estimated to be 45 mph.
Willacy County Sheriffs Office reported estimated wind gusts of 60 mph at their location.
Willacy County Emergency Manager reported two power poles down and two power poles damaged along Highway 186 near the wind turbine farm west of San Perlita.

Police officer reported golfball sized hail in the city of San Perlita.
Willacy County Emergency Manager reported a telephone pole blown down on FM 1015 in the town of Lasara and a power line down in Raymondville, near the intersection of TX 186 and Business 77.
Willacy County EM reported golf ball size hail in Port Mansfield.
A couple of utility poles were reported down along FM 491, approximately one mile west of Business 77.
Large tree reported down via social media. Time estimated based on radar.

The Emergency Management Coordinator from Willacy County, Texas, reported a small tornado briefly touched down between Raymondville and San Perlita. There was no structural damage, but patches of sugar cane were blown down based on photo evidence, and a short video confirmed the …

The Emergency Management Coordinator for Willacy County reported damage to eight utility poles and 20 to 30 mesquite trees on the I-69E Frontage Road near the intersection with Conley Road, north of Raymondville. The utility pole damage was a combination of those uprooted from th…

Numerous large mesquite and a few large ash tree limbs, including some uprooted trees, were seen on an NWS Storm Survey in western Willacy County from State Highway 186 about 8 miles west of Raymondville through and just south of Lasara along FM-1015. A few power lines were also …
One roof was blown off a residence in Raymondville, and there were several calls to dispatch of trees and power poles down between Raymondville and Lyford.

A mini-supercell thunderstorm rolled through central and southeastern Willacy County a little more than an hour after sunrise, and produced damaging winds near San Perlita and on nearby ranches around 830 AM CDT. One residence in San Perlita, fully exposed to the northwest, susta…
Law enforcement reported dime-sized hail in the city of Raymondville as thunderstorms moved through the area. Time frame is estimated.
The Willacy County Sheriff's Department reported hail up to the size of nickels in Raymondville as storms moved through the area. Time frame is estimated.
Several reports from social media of ping pong ball to hen egg, or two inch, hail just south of the Lyford area to the Cameron/Willacy County line.
Multiple reports of 0.5 to 2.0 hail in the Sebastian area.

A Willacy County Emergency Manager reported a power pole and lines down at 1425 N 490 in Raymondville.
There were several videos and pictures sent to the local news media of nickel size hail.
